PullRequest.Title: test: isolate CAPI replay from debugger discovery probes
PullRequest.Body:

Extracted from #344572 so the replay harness fix can be reviewed and merged independently of Connector routing.

Local dbgjs discovery scans listening HTTP ports for DevTools targets. Those probes reached the CAPI replay proxy, causing strict replay to report unrecorded `GET /json/version` requests during teardown even though all prompt assertions passed. The source was confirmed by tracing the incoming connection to dbgjs's discovery process.

Return HTTP 404 for `GET /json/version` and `GET /json/list` before record/replay processing. These probes are neither forwarded upstream nor captured in recordings. All other unknown API requests and unrecorded model requests retain strict cache-miss behavior. No fixtures or snapshots change.

Adds regression tests for both recording and replay, strictness checks, and troubleshooting documentation.

### Validation

On this standalone branch, without the Connector changes:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxy.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxyPathNormalization.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxyShellTools.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, **23 tests**.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotBuiltinToolAllowlist.integrationTest.ts --reporter dot` - passed, **25 tests**, including teardown.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

The identical proxy changes also passed `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/harness/capiReplayProxy.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxy.test.ts` before extraction; commit hygiene hooks passed. Validation was local on macOS, not cross-platform CI.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local debugger discovery probes GET /json/version and GET /json/list against a running replay proxy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The HTTP server parses the request URL and immediately drains the request and returns 404. No fixture lookup, replay matching, body concatenation, or record-mode forwarding must complete before the probe receives its response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive a loopback HTTP discovery request and return HTTP 404.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loopback request/response per probed endpoint, normally two requests per scan of this proxy port.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The loopback request already reached the proxy, but it continued through body buffering and record/replay dispatch rather than receiving the dedicated early 404.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The 404 is the complete critical path and now completes before record/replay processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward unknown requests to the configured CAPI or mock upstream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one outbound request per debugger probe in record mode; after the diff, zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each discovery probe in record mode could be forwarded upstream because it was not an ancillary stub; the early return now prevents that fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This network boundary was previously on the record-mode probe path and is now removed from it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the replay fixture once at proxy construction or write the recording fixture once at shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fixture read for the replay proxy and one fixture write for the recording proxy, independent of probe count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lifecycle I/O occurred, though record-mode probes could add exchanges to processing before the final write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixture loading precedes serving replay probes; recording fixture writing occurs at shutdown and is not needed before the 404 response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two known endpoint probes per discovery scan for each listening proxy port; repeated scans scale linearly with debugger discovery frequency. There is no cache or grouping, but each request is handled independently with constant work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node's HTTP server may accept overlapping probes without an explicit limiter; each changed-path probe performs only synchronous URL parsing plus nonblocking request drain and response completion. No asynchronous upstream operations are spawned after the change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The changed probe path bypasses replay buckets and recording state entirely. Warm versus cold fixture state does not affect it; no positive or negative cache entry is created. Replay construction still loads its fixture once, and record shutdown still writes its fixture once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard returns before body listeners and before both _replay and _record, so the removed processing and upstream boundary are explicit in the call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Debugger scan frequency varies by local tooling, but the changed mechanism unambiguously removes rather than adds downstream work for each matching probe.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The change shortens the probe critical path and eliminates record-mode boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal ancillary and model traffic through the CAPI replay proxy during agent-host integration tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every request now performs one initial URL parse before the existing body collection. Replay then uses in-memory fixture buckets and response generation; recording forwards one request upstream and buffers the response for fixture generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward record-mode SDK traffic to a mock or real upstream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outbound request per non-stub recorded request, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was buffered and forwarded once; only the preliminary URL parsing/check was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The upstream response remains on the recording critical path; the added URL parse occurs before it but does not change boundary count or concurrency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load replay YAML or serialize and write recording YAML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per proxy construction/reset and one write per recording proxy shutdown, unchanged by request cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replay loading occurs before request handling; recording serialization/write occurs during stop. The diff does not move either operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and parse a URL to extract the pathname for the debugger-probe check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once newly added per incoming ordinary request, in addition to existing downstream parsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary requests entered body collection directly and parsed their URL only in the downstream managed-settings, replay, or record handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A small synchronous allocation/parse occurs on the request path before body collection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of SDK HTTP requests in an integration scenario. The diff adds one URL object/path extraction per request; managed-settings requests parse the URL again in the existing special case, and replay/record requests parse it again in their existing handlers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests are accepted by the Node HTTP server without a shared limiter. The diff does not add promises, queues, subprocesses, or outbound requests, so aggregate network concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay fixtures are loaded into in-memory buckets at construction/reset and consumed by key; ordinary replay remains warm after loading and never contacts upstream. Recording remains uncached and forwards each request. The new probe comparison neither invalidates nor bypasses caches for non-probe traffic.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one URL parse/allocation is added per request; high that no expensive boundary count, scheduling, or retained lifecycle changes for ordinary traffic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Integration scenarios vary in request count, but this is test-only traffic and the added operation is a bounded parse of the short request URL, dwarfed by existing HTTP, body, fixture, and model-processing work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The only added ordinary-request cost is a constant, short URL parse in a test harness, with no realistic material latency, throughput, or memory impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: New CapiReplayProxy regression tests for probe exclusion and strict replay preservation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tests sequentially start local proxies, issue fixed loopback fetches, consume each response, stop each proxy, and perform bounded fixture assertions and temporary-directory cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start loopback HTTP servers and issue fetch requests to them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Eight fixed loopback requests across six fixed proxy lifecycles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These regression cases and their loopback requests did not run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each fetch response is awaited before the test advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/remove one temporary directory and read/write a small empty capture fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary directory lifecycle, one recording write, and bounded small fixture reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test suite did not perform this specific temporary fixture lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These synchronous filesystem operations occur on the test critical path but have fixed tiny cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality: two proxy modes times two probe endpoints, plus four strictness cases. No data-dependent collection or unbounded history controls the work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All proxy starts and fetches are awaited sequentially. No Promise.all burst or subprocess is introduced; each proxy is stopped before the next relevant iteration proceeds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The record pass writes one temporary empty fixture, the replay pass loads it, and each strictness case loads the committed empty fixture into a fresh proxy. There is no cross-test cache, but the total is fixed and intentional for lifecycle isolation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: test loops and awaits establish exact cardinality and serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and loopback latency vary by CI host, but the fixed eight requests and small fixture operations cannot scale with product input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The added regression coverage has small, fixed test-only cost and no burst, leak, or scaling mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced matching probes, ordinary proxy traffic, and the added tests through URL parsing, fixture I/O, loopback HTTP, and record-mode upstream forwarding. The PR removes expensive downstream work for debugger probes and adds only bounded test coverage plus a negligible per-request parse for ordinary test-harness traffic; no reportable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
